questions.solution:
Vector $\vec{P}=a \hat{i}+a \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}$ and vector $\vec{Q}=a \hat{i}-2 \hat{j}-\hat{k}$.
If two vectors are perpendicular to each other, then

\vec{P} \cdot \vec{Q}=0 \quad \text { or } \quad(a \hat{i}+a \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}) \cdot(a \hat{i}-2 \hat{j}-\hat{k})=0

or $a^2-2 a-3=0$.
Solving this quadratic equation, we get $a=3$ or -1 . Therefore positive value of $a$ is 3 .

questions.q: The kinetic energy of a body becomes four times its initial value. The new linear momentum will be
options: four times of the initial value
eight times of the initial value.
questions.solution:
Initial kinetic energy $\left(E_1\right)=E$ and final kinetic energy $\left(E_2\right)=4 E$.
Kinetic energy of a body is $\frac{1}{2} m v^2$
Since the value of $m$ remains constant, therefore for the kinetic energy to be 4 times, the new value of velocity (v) should be 2 times the initial value. Initial linear momentum $\left(p_1\right)=m v$.
Therefore new linear momentum $\left(p_2\right)=m \times 2 v=2 m v=2 p_1$

questions.q: The density of a substance at $0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is $10 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cc}$ and at $100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, its density is $9.7 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cc}$. The coefficient of linear expansion of the substance is

Initial density $\left(\rho_1\right)=10 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cc}$
Final temperature $\left(T_2\right)=100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and
Final density $\left(\rho_2\right)=9.7 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cc}$.
Coefficient of volumetric expansion $\left(\alpha_v\right)=\frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho_1 \times \Delta T}$
=\frac{\rho_1-\rho_2}{\rho_1\left(T_2-T_1\right)}=\frac{10-9.7}{10(100-0)}=\frac{0.3}{1000}=3 \times 10^{-4} \text {. }

Therefore coefficient of linear expansion,

\alpha_1=\frac{\gamma}{3}=\frac{3 \times 10^{-4}}{3}=10^{-4}

questions.q: The velocities of sound at the same temperature in two monoatomic gases of densities $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ are $v_1$ and $v_2$ respectively. If $\rho_1 / \rho_2=4$, then the value of $v_1 / v_2$ is
questions.solution:
Velocity of sound in the gas of density $\rho_1$ is $v_1$ and velocity of sound in the gas of density $\rho_2$ is $v_2$.

Therefore $\frac{v_1}{v_2}=\sqrt{\frac{\rho_2}{\rho_1}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}}=\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a wire is stretched and its radius becomes $r / 2$, then its resistance will be
questions.solution:
Initial radius of wire, $r_1=r$ and final radius of wire, $r_2=r / 2=0.5 r$.
Since volume of the wire after stretch remains constant, therefore $l_1 A_1=l_2 A_2$
or

\frac{l_1}{l_2}=\frac{A_2}{A_1}=\frac{r_2^2}{r_1^2}=\left(\frac{0.5 r}{r}\right)^2=\frac{1}{4} .

The resistance $(R)=\rho \frac{l}{A} \propto \frac{l}{A}$.
Therefore $\frac{R_1}{R_2}=\frac{l_1}{l_2} \times \frac{A_2}{A_1}=\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{16}$ or $\quad R_2=16 R_1=16 R$.

We also know that when the plane of the armature is parallel to the lines of force of magnetic field, the rate of change of magnetic flux linked with it is maximum. Therefore the e.m.f. induced in the armature in this orientation is maximum.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Methyl orange is the example of which type of dye?
questions.solution: Methyl orange belongs to the group of azo dyes. It is also acidic in nature due to presence of sulphonic group.

If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.

questions.solution:
In the cell, DNA molecules (i.e. Deoxyribose Nucleic acid) are present predominatly in the nucleus, some DNA is also present in the mitochondria in Eukaryotes.
RNA molecules (i.e. Ribose nucleic acid) are present in cytoplasm of the eukaryotes and in nucleus in some prokaryotes and virus.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The vitamin nicotinamide can be synthesized in our body from
questions.solution: The amino acid tryptophan serves as a source material for the synthesis of nicotinamide which in turn forms two coenzymes NAD and NADP with metabolic roles.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following would not give Fehling's test ?
questions.solution: Fehling's test is given only by reducing sugars. When Fehling's solution is added to any reducing sugar then a red precipitate is formed which shows that reduction has taken place. Sucrose does not give this test.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Systematics is the branch of biology that deals with classification of living organism.
Reason : The aim of classification is to group the organisms in an orderly manner.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Taxonomy or systematics is the branch of biology that deals with the classification of biological world of living organisms. The classification is the grouping of organisms in an orderly manner. This grouping is based upon similarities and dissimilarities.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following structures helps in the respiration of lichens?
questions.solution: Cyphella are small depressions or cavity like openings into the medulla on the ventral surface of the thallus of certain lichens. They perform respiratory functions.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : In bacteria, photosynthesis occurs by utilizing wavelengths longer than $700 \mathrm{~nm}$. 
Reason : Here the reaction centre is B-890.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: In bacteria, the reaction centre is B-890 and photosynthesis occurs by utilizing wavelengths longer than $700 \mathrm{~nm}$. The reductant is $\mathrm{NADH}+\mathrm{H}^{+}$. In bacteria, the donor may be hydrogen sulphide etc, but not water.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Plasmids are double stranded extrachromosomal DNA.
Reason : Plasmids are possessed by eukaryotic cells.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Plasmids are found mostly in prokaryotic cells and yeasts. They do not form a part of the normal chromosomal DNA of a cell and are capable of replicating independently. They constitute extrachromosomal DNA.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Algae are useful because they
options: are used in curdling of milk.
questions.solution: Maximum solar energy is trapped by algae and hence they evolve maximum amount of oxygen by the process of photosynthesis. Therefore, algae are useful because they purify the atmosphere by releasing oxygen.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The plant body of moss (Funaria) is
questions.solution: The gametophytic generation represents the dominant phase in the life cycle of bryophytes. The sporophyte phase is dependent on the gametophyte. That is why, the plant body of Funaria moss is predominantly gametophytic with dependent sporophyte.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Elater mechanism for seed dispersal is exhibited by
questions.solution: Marchantia is a liverwort. Its sporophyte contains elongated cells with spiral thickenings on its wall called elaters. These elaters are hygroscopic in nature. The resulting twisting movement helps in dispersal of spores.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Ambulacral grooves are absent in the living forms of the Class
questions.solution: Ambulacral grooves are found in the arms of echinoderms lined by tube feet. Ambulacral grooves are absent in Ophiuroidea which are covered by ossicles.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: No Solution Available

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Hydra receives impulses and stimuli through
questions.solution: In Hydra sensory cells are found in the gastrodermis. They are supposed to be stimulated by the entry of the prey into the gastrovascular cavity.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Lateral line system is found in fishes and aquatic larval amphibians.
Reason : Lateral line system has receptors which are the clusters of sensory cells derived from ectoderm.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Lateral line system is a sensory system of fishes and aquatic and larval amphibians whose receptors are clusters of sensory cells derived from ectoderm. These clusters of sensory cells are called neuromast organs.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: When the filament runs throughout the length of anther, it is called
questions.solution: In adnate type filament attachment, the filament runs throughout the length of anther. It is found in Ranunculus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : The two cotyledons in the seed are often referred to as the embryonic leaves.
Reason : The embryo contains radicle and plumule.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: In a typical angiospermic plant, cotyledons in the seed are the embryonic leaves. The radicle of the embryo upon the seed germination produces the root system and the plumule produces the shoot system. The radicle and plumule are contained in the embryo.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Passage cells are found in
questions.solution: nocot root. It is an unthickened cell in the endodermis of a root, found opposite to the protoxylem element through which solutions can diffuse in the transverse direction.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : The collenchyma is a thick walled living tissue.
Reason : The collenchyma is thickened due to the deposition of pectin.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Collenchyma is a specialized type of parenchyma which functions as supporting tissue. The cell walls are irregularly thickened due to the deposition of cellulose and pectin. It is a living tissue.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : The number of cells in a multicellular organism is inversely proportional to the size of body. 
Reason : All the cells in the biological world are of same size.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: The number of cells in a multicellular organism are directly proportional to the size of the body. On the other hand, it is a fact that cells vary greatly in their size.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is related to glycosylation of protein?
questions.solution: Glycosylation is bonding of sugar residue to another organic compound. Glycoproteins are formed in the lumen of rough endoplasmic reticulum, but may subsequently be modified in the lumen of the Golgi apparatus, where other amino acids of the protein may become glycosylated.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A chromosome carrying the centromere at one of the ends is called
questions.solution: If centromere is truly terminal, i.e. situated at the tip of chromosome, the chromosome is said to be telocentric. Telocentric chromosomes are very rare.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Specialization of cells is advantageous for the organism.
Reason : It increases the operational efficiency of an organism.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Specialization of cells into tissue, organ and organ systems is advantageous for the organism. It increases the operational efficiency through division of labour which avoids duplication of work.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Bud dormancy is induced by
questions.solution: The bud dormancy is induced by adantscissic acid (ABA). The level of endogenous ABA increases with the onset of dormant period and decreases when it is broken.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Death is regarded as the most important regulatory process on earth.
Reason : It avoids overcrowding, caused by continuous reproduction.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Death is regarded as the most important regulatory process on earth. It reduces the number of individuals in a population and avoids overcrowding caused by continuous reproduction. Overcrowding due to reproduction is countered by death as the ultimate termination of functional life.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: If turgor pressure becomes equal to the wall pressure, then
options: no exchange of water takes place
solute goes from the cell into water.
questions.solution: The pressure that develops in a cell from time to time due to osmotic diffusion of water molecules into a cell that causes stretching of the cell wall is called turgor pressure. Due to turgor pressure, rigid cell wall offers resistance. This resistance works in a direction opposite to turgor pressure. But it is equal to turgor pressure and is called wall pressure. In this condition, no exchange of water takes place.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Glycolysis is found in cytoplasm of virtually all types of aerobic/anaerobic cells. In this process, glucose is converted into
questions.solution: In glycolysis one molecule of hexose sugar (glucose/fructose), a 6C-compound is splitted to form two molecules of a $3 \mathrm{C}$-compound, pyruvic acid $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COCOOH}\right)$.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The photorespiratory carbon-oxidation cycle involves the interaction of
questions.solution: Photorespiration is a metabolic pathway that occurs in plants in the presence of light, in which ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase the (RuBisCO) enzyme involved in carbon dioxide fixation with ribulose bisphosphate, accepts oxygen, in place of carbon dioxide, resulting in the formation of a twocarbon compound, glycolate. Most of the fixed carbon represented by the glycolate can be salvaged by a series of reactions-the glycolate pathway - involving the peroxisomes and mitochondria, and returned to the chloroplasts. However, some of the carbon is lost as carbon dioxide. Unlike respiration there is no production of ATP.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : When six molecules of carbon dioxide participate in photosynthesis, 12 molecules of $\mathrm{NADP}^{+}$and $18 \mathrm{ATP}$ are used up, forming one hexose molecule.
Reason : The photosynthetic light reaction results in the formation of ATP and NADPH.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: When six molecules of carbon dioxide enter Calvin cycle, one hexose molecule is formed, whereas 18 ATP and $12 \mathrm{NADP}^{+}$molecules are used up. The light reaction of photosynthesis results in the formation of ATP and NADPH.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Xenia and metaxenia terms are related with
questions.solution: The direct or indirect effect of male parent (pollen grain) on structures inside embryo sac except embryo has been termed by Focke, 1881 as xenia. This phenomenon is limited to endosperm part only and is seen in Zea mays. Metaxenia may be defined as the effect of pollen on the seed coat or pericarp lying outside the embryo sac. In Phoenix dactylifera, the size and time of maturity of fruits depend on the type of pollen grains fertilising the ovules. There is secretion of certain hormones or similar substances by endosperm or embryo or both which diffuse out into the wall of the seed and fruit and exert specific effect. The secretion of these substances, in turn, is influenced by the pollen grains which fertilise the ovules.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Megasporophyll of Cycas has the same nature as
questions.solution: Megasporophyll of Cycas are borne on female plant which produces ovule. Carpel is also a female reproductive organ of flowering plant. So both are of same nature. (i.e. female sex organs).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : The megaspore mother cell undergoes mitosis to produce four megaspores.
Reason : Megaspore mother cells and the megaspores are both haploid.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.

questions.solution: The diploid megaspore mother cell has a large nucleus and dense cytoplasm. This cell undergoes meiosis (reduction division) to produce a group of four haploid cells called megaspores.

options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: The advancement in the field of biology has reached to such an extent that it requires the basic knowledge of chemistry, physics and other basic sciences. It is a fact that living organisms are made up of atoms and molecules which follow chemical and physical laws. Therefore knowledge of chemistry and physics is essential for studying biology.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Living organisms are regarded as closed systems.
Reason : Energy of living organisms cannot be lost or gained from the environment.
options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Living organisms are regarded as open systems as they can lose or gain the mass or energy from the surrounding environment. All living organisms restore their lost energy either from the sunlight or indirectly from the food material.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Green muffler is used against which type of pollution ?
questions.solution: Green plants are being planted around the road side to check the noise pollution. This is known as green muffler. Noise pollution is measured in decibels.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution: In cockroach, excretion is mainly performed by one or two pairs of malpighian tubules. One of this pair opens into the middle region of intestine and other pair of coxal glands are located in prosoma and opens at bases of fifth walking legs.

questions.solution: In frog, all nerve cells connecting to central nervous system (brain and spinal cord) with receptor and effectors constitute the peripheral nervous system. Some small masses of nerve cell bodies are called ganglia. They develop from neural crest cells in frog.

questions.solution: The premolars and molars are called cheek teeth. These are also called lophodont teeth. Their free ends are flattened and bear transverse ridges to crush and grind the food.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following digestive juices has the minimum $\mathrm{pH}$ value?
questions.solution: Bile is an alkaline viscous fluid, yellow to green in colour and having a $\mathrm{pH}$ of 7.8-8.6. Saliva is secreted by salivary gland and its $\mathrm{pH}$ is about 6.8 . Gastric juice is secreted by the gastric gland in stomach and its $\mathrm{pH}$ value is 1-2.5 and pancreatic juice is colourless watery fluid and slightly alkaline. Its $\mathrm{pH}$ is $7.5-8.0$. Therefore gastric juice has minimum $\mathrm{pH}$ value.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution: Rennin is an enzyme found in gastric juices responsible for the coagulation of milk. It acts by hydrolysing peptide links.

If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.

questions.solution: During a wound, germs are removed by the process of phagocytosis by WBC. WBCs accumulate at the site of wound by diapedesis. Diapedesis is the squeezing of leucocytes out from the endothelium of capillaries to fight against foreign agent.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Assertion : The regulation of RBC production is accompanied by the kidneys.
Reason : Erythropoietin hormone circulates to the red bone marrow, where it increases stem cell mitosis and speeds up the development of RBCs.

questions.subject: Zoology

Assertion : Histamine is involved in allergic and inflammatory reactions.

options: If both the assertion and reason are true and reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but assertion is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
If the assertion is true but the reason is false.

questions.solution: Histamine is a derivative of the amino acid histidine produced by damaged cells of vertebrates. When released, it has the effect of dilating capillaries and lowering blood pressure. Histamine is involved in allergic and inflammatory reactions.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following are uricotelic animals?
questions.solution: Uricotelic animals (living in dry conditions) are those animals which excrete uric acid as their excretory product e.g. lizard and crow. These animals conserve water in their bodies and synthesize crystals of uric acids from ammonia. These crystals can be retained in the body (in solid form) for a considerable time before being discharged from the body.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The cranial capacity was largest among the
questions.solution: Neanderthal man was the first human fossil discovered in 1856 having a cranial capacity of 1400 cc. African man (Australopithecus) was discovered in 1924 having a cranial capacity of $300-500 \mathrm{cc}$. Java ape man (Pithecanthropus erectus) was discovered in 1920 and its cranial capacity was $900 \mathrm{cc}$ whereas Peking man (Sinanthropus pekinensis) was discovered in 1924 and its cranial capacity was $1100 \mathrm{cc}$. These show that Neanderthal man has the largest cranial capacity.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution: Wuchereria bancrofii is a dreaded human parasite. It is digenetic parasite completing its life cycle in two hosts, the final host is man harbouring the adult worm. The adult worms live coiled up in the gland and lymph vessels of man.
